title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Top of the page. This finishes the previous page's definition of when a finite family of cylindrical neighbourhoods (B_i, E_{B_i}) of strata is transversal to a conic neighbourhood T of Y ⊂ X. The requirement is that, for every finite J, E_J ∩ T is conic over T. The induced conic structure should be the product, with the corner factor I^J (unit intervals indexed by J), of a conic structure on the pair (T_J, Y_J), where T_J = T ∩ B_J and Y_J = Y ∩ B_J. Ṫ_J should be the boundary part of the cone over Y_J. In modern terms, the corner coordinates coming from the cylindrical (collar) neighbourhoods split off as a product factor compatible with the conic (mapping-cylinder) structure of the tubular neighbourhood. This is a compatibility of control data, of Mather type, between collars of boundary faces and conic tubes.

§6, relations with stratifications of type I, where I is a finite ordered set. A stratification of type I of X is an increasing family (X_i), i ∈ I, of closed subspaces. It is called 'privileged' if three conditions hold.
(a) For each covering relation j' → j (j a successor of j'), X_{j'} ⊂ X_j is a 'bordant' embedding, i.e. a collared boundary-type inclusion.
(b) For fixed j, the X_{j'} with j' an immediate predecessor of j form a family of mutually transversal collared boundary pieces of X_j, transversal in the sense of the previous page.
(c) For every i ≤ j, the interval I_{ij} = [i, j] has the structure of the face poset of a simplex. Precisely, let S be the set of immediate predecessors of j in I_{ij}, i.e. the maximal elements of I_{ij} \ {j}. For k ∈ I_{ij} put s_k = {s ∈ S : k ≤ s}. Then k ↦ s_k is decreasing and is an anti-isomorphism I_{ij} ≅ P(S)^op. So every interval is a Boolean lattice, with i ↔ S and j ↔ ∅.
A marginal NB says that, given (c), some existence hypothesis is automatic.

The next page draws the consequence. The local structure of X_j along X_i is the 'cubical' case: a corner of a cube of dimension n = card S. It also proves a diamond lemma: Inf(K, J') exists and is a predecessor of K. This lets one compare the bordant pairs (X_K, X_{K'}) → (X_J, X_{J'}).

Purpose. Inside the programme of 'déploiement' (unfolding) of stratified spaces, this axiomatizes the kind of stratified space that the unfolding produces: a manifold-with-corners-like object whose faces are indexed by a poset with Boolean intervals. The aim is to relate conic neighbourhoods of strata to such corner structures.
errors: The definition is a sketch with crossed-out alternatives. Condition (b) is left grammatically unfinished on the page.
The marginal claim that, given (c), an existence hypothesis is 'automatic' is not justified on this page.

Boolean intervals are a local poset condition. No global condition (e.g. existence of infima) is imposed; the next page has to add the hypothesis 'there exists i below K and J'' to get Inf(K, J'). The definition as stated does not give lattice-like behaviour globally. This is not an error, but the definition depends on such auxiliary hypotheses.

ideas.what: Transversality of a family of collars/cylindrical neighbourhoods with a conic neighbourhood: E_J ∩ T ≅ (cone structure on (T_J, Y_J)) × I^J
ideas.modern_name: Compatible control data / corner-compatible tubular neighbourhoods in Thom–Mather theory; boundary-defining functions compatible with radial structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mather (1970), Thom; Verona (1984) for abstract stratified sets with corners
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 only alludes to tame spaces and tubular neighbourhoods

ideas.what: Stratification indexed by a finite poset I with bordant (collared boundary) inclusions for covering relations, and every interval [i, j] anti-isomorphic to P(S) (face poset of a simplex / cube corner)
ideas.modern_name: Manifolds with faces / ⟨n⟩-manifolds; poset-stratified manifolds with corners; Boolean-interval posets (cf. Stanley's simplicial posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jänich (1968, ⟨n⟩-manifolds), Laures (2000), Douady (1961, variétés à bord anguleux); Stanley (1991) for the poset notion

ideas.what: Using such corner-stratified spaces as the target of the 'déploiement' (unfolding / resolution) of a conically stratified space
ideas.modern_name: Resolution of Thom–Mather stratified spaces into manifolds with corners (iterated fibration structures, unzipping)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 mentions the programme of tame topology and dévissage of stratified structures, but not this formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck (1981-82) gives a poset-indexed definition of a 'privileged' stratification modelled on manifolds with corners: bordant inclusions along covering relations, plus every interval being Boolean (a simplex face poset). This is intended as the codomain of unfolding stratified spaces. The definition is close to later Verona / Albin–Mazzeo et al. / Ayala–Francis–Tanaka formalisms of resolution to manifolds with corners, and to the interval-wise Boolean condition on face posets.
missed.quote: la structure de l'ens. des k tels que i ≤ k ≤ j est celle de l'ens. des faces d'un simplexe ... l'application k ↦ s_k (qui est décroissante) est un anti-isomorphisme de I_ij sur P(S)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows an independent early formulation of the combinatorics (Boolean intervals, diamond lemma on the next page) underlying the resolution of stratified spaces into manifolds with corners. It may be of historical interest for the exit-path / unzipping literature. Mathematically it is largely subsumed by later work.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, early (1981-82), poset-theoretic axiomatization of corner-type stratifications as the output of unfolding stratified spaces. The ideas closely match later published work (Verona 1984, Jänich's ⟨n⟩-manifolds earlier), so it is a notable unpublished detail rather than a missing result.
transcription_corrections: Line 'est celle de l'un ... variation d'un simplexe' should most likely read 'est celle de l'ens. des faces d'un simplexe'. The struck-out word is 'simplexe', with 'un simplexe' rewritten above.
'i.e. des éléments minimaux de I_ij \ {j}' is probably 'maximaux'. Immediate predecessors of j are the maximal elements of I_ij \ {j}; the handwriting is ambiguous.

Condition (b) reads roughly: 'j fixé, j' variable parmi les prédécesseurs, les X_{j'} sont des sous-espaces bordants transversaux de X_j'. The text 'j'voudrait' is a misreading of j' plus a following word.
First line: 'E_J ∩ T conique sur T, et la structure conique induite est la structure produit par I^J d'une structure conique sur (T_J, Y_J)'. The factor is I^J, not İ^J.
